1 CAUSE JUDGE & 32ND ACMM MEMBER, MACT-3, BENGALURU,
PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This is an appeal filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation aggrieved by the award passed in M.V.C.No.3748/2016 dated 26.07.2017 by the Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal.
The claim petition was filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the claimant in the road accident.

2. It is the case of the claimant that on 02.04.2016 at about 7:50 p.m., when she was waiting for the bus at the Bus stand on extreme edge of the road at 5th Cross Junction, Magadi Road, Bengaluru, at that time a car came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and NC: 2023:KHC:41474 dashed against the claimant, due to which she fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. As per the wound certificate, the claimant had sustained 1) laceration present over back of right elbow,
2) laceration present over postero-lateral aspect of upper third of right leg, 3) swelling, tenderness and deformity over right leg and 4) abrasion present over front of right knee.
The doctor has opined that injury Nos.1, 2 and 4 are simple in nature and injury No.3 is grievous in nature.
4. The Court below under the head of pain and agony had granted an amount of Rs.40,000/-.

When it comes to the loss of income during the treatment period, according to the claimant, she was working as Team Leader at Atcis Company, Bengaluru and was earning an amount of Rs.15,000/-
per month.
As there was no evidence, the Court below had taken an amount of Rs.7,500/- as the income per month and for 3 months, granted an amount of Rs.22,500/-.

When it comes to loss NC:
2023:KHC:41474 of future earnings, doctor has deposed that there is 51% disability to the lower limb and 26% disability to the whole body.
The Court below had taken 12% as the disability to the whole body and granted compensation of an amount of Rs.1,83,600/-.
When it comes to the medical expenses, the Court below had granted an amount of Rs.88,424/-.
The Court below had granted an amount of Rs.20,000/- under the head of loss of amenities, conveyance, food and nourishment and attendant charges.

Towards future medical expenses, the doctor had stated that the claimant has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants and would require an amount of Rs.40,000/-
and the Court below had granted an amount of Rs.15,000/-.
Altogether, compensation of an amount of Rs.3,69,524/- was awarded.

sentences.text: Learned counsel appearing for the claimant submits that she had sustained so many injuries and under the head of pain and suffering, granting an amount of Rs.40,000/- is on the lower side.
It is submitted that NC: 2023:KHC:41474 the doctor has clearly stated that there is 26% disability to the whole body and the Court below had taken 12% as the disability without any basis.
He further submits that the compensation that was granted by the Court below towards loss of income during the laid up period and future earning was not reasonable.

It is submitted that under the head of loss of amenities, conveyance, food and nourishment and attendant charges, the Court below had granted an amount of Rs.20,000/-, which is also not a reasonable compensation.
It is submitted that the doctor has deposed that the claimant requires an amount of Rs.40,000/- towards future surgery and the Court below had granted only an amount of Rs.15,000/-.
Learned counsel submits that the compensation that was awarded by the Tribunal was not just and reasonable.

6. On the other hand, learned Government Pleader appearing for the respondents submits that the Court below considering one grievous injury had rightly granted an amount of Rs.40,000/- towards pain and agony.
He NC: 2023:KHC:41474 submits that the Court below had rightly taken 12% as disability to the whole body and 26% disability as stated by the doctor is on the higher side.
He submits that the claimant was earning an amount of Rs.15,000/- per month.
But, as no evidence was placed by the claimant, the Court below had rightly taken an amount of Rs.7,500/- as the income per month.

It is submitted that the compensation granted is reasonable and no grounds are made out for enhancement of the compensation.
7.
Having heard the learned counsel on either side, perused the entire material on record.
The claimant had sustained altogether 4 injuries and as per the wound certificate, 3 injuries are simple in nature and 1 injury is grievous in nature.

The Court below had granted an amount of Rs.40,000/-
under the head of pain and agony and this Court finds no reason to interfere.
Then coming to the loss of income during the laid up period, as there was no evidence, an amount of Rs.7,500/- was taken as the income of the claimant.

Considering that this is an NC: 2023:KHC:41474 accident of the year 2016, this Court is inclined to take an amount of Rs.9,500/- as the income per month and for 3 months, the claimant is entitled for an amount of Rs.28,500/- under the head of loss of income during the laid up period.
Coming to the disability, as per the doctor, it is 51% to the lower limb and 1/3rd of it is calculated as 17%.
This Court is inclined to take 17% as the disability to the whole body.
Hence, under the head of loss of future earning due to disability, it would come to Rs.9,500x12x17x17/100 = Rs.3,29,460/-.
Coming to the medical expenses, the Court below had granted an amount of Rs.88,424/- and this Court finds no reason to interfere.

Under the head of loss of amenities, the claimant is entitled for an amount of Rs.20,000/- and under the head of transport, conveyance and attendant charges, this Court is inclined to grant another amount of Rs.15,000/-.
Towards future medical expenses, considering that this is an accident of year 2016, this Court is inclined to grant an amount of Rs.20,000/-.

In the light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of V.MEKALA vs. M.
MALATHI AND ANOTHER1, the claimant is entitled for an amount of Rs.10,000/- towards legal expenses.

No costs.
